facts.statement: The genus Eutreptodactylus was described by Baird and Vickers-Rich in 1997.
Eutreptodactylus was an extinct bird that lived in Brazil during the Early Eocene period.
facts.quote: Eutreptodactylus is an extinct genus of insectivorous bird known from the Early Eocene period (Itaboraian) of Brazil.
Eutreptodactylus is an extinct genus of insectivorous bird

facts.statement: Fossils of Eutreptodactylus have been found in the Itaboraí Formation at São José de Itaborai.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Itaboraí Formation at São José de Itaborai.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Eutreptodactylus is the family Cuculidae.
Eutreptodactylus lived between 56 and 48.07 million years ago during the Ypresian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Researchers suggest that Eutreptodactylus was likely the most primitive member of the order Cuculiformes.
rejected.quote: It was probably the most primitive member of the order Cuculiformes.

rejected.statement: Eutreptodactylus belongs to the class Aves.
